q1_issues.issue: The consequent stacks (Past (sk_buy $x)) beside (Can (sk_buy $x)), so the rule derives for every person a specific past buying of the land as separate conjuncts, whereas the sentence asserts only that such a purchase was possible — the instruction set's own capability example ("Bob can cook dinner") deliberately leaves the event tenseless, which is the unmarked generic/dispositional default.

q2_gaps: free-choice "anyone" as a universal quantifier — the quantifier-to-strength table covers all/every, most, a lot of, many, few, no/none, but not any/anyone, so neither the strength (here 1.0) nor the QuantifierPhrase surface string (here "any" for surface "anyone") is specified

past-oriented modality "could have V-ed" — no licensed way to scope the past over the modality rather than over the event; and the routing is underdetermined, since the capability-generic redirect sends a kind-ranging "can V" to the reified (Inheritance kind (can <action>)) property, which cannot carry a past time anchor or a specific definite object
notes: The instruction set pulls two ways: the Epistemic bullet licenses putting the perfect inside a modal ("might have cleared"), while *Quantifiers, generics & scope* routes a kind-level capability away from the event-rule form entirely. Everything else follows the instruction set exactly — the Skolem-function distribution rule at 1.0/0.9, Theme for "buy", the definite "the land" typed outside the rule, and (BeforeBy (sk_buy $x) now 50 year) for the "N units ago" anchor.
